about: Homework for this pillar, one list per AI (Claude writes it; tools/kit/render.py in jpavia10/prometheus-hub turns it into docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md and the Drive docs). Every task says exactly what to read, what to make, how many, where to save it, how Claude checks it and what makes it not done. A task is done only when the file passes the checks, never because it was sent.

tasks.title: TRIAL 3: what makes the home screen and Athenaeum slow on a phone (find it from the code)
tasks.why: TRIAL (do these first, in this order): a measured test of what this model can do; scored against answers or measurements Claude holds, not by opinion. Reading a large codebase and reasoning about what a browser does every frame. Claude measured both pages at phone size with the CPU slowed 4x: the home screen holds about 33 frames a second at rest even with its WebGL canvases hidden, Athenaeum about 47; both should hold 60. Claude has found part of the cause; you are scored on what you find that its measurements confirm.
tasks.unlocks: The fixes go into the next motion pass; the home screen and Athenaeum are the two pages Joseph opens most.
inputs: https://github.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/tree/74e34cf3c30adede4defdb67c00a2a90ea1fa1cb/deck (home: index at the repository root loads deck/app.js, deck/deck.css, deck/views/menu.js, deck/core/atmo.js, deck/core/fx.js and the rest)

https://github.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/tree/74e34cf3c30adede4defdb67c00a2a90ea1fa1cb/pillars/athenaeum and https://github.com/jpavia10/prometheus-hub/tree/74e34cf3c30adede4defdb67c00a2a90ea1fa1cb/kit (the shared kit every pillar loads)
steps: Read the code at commit 74e34cf (the links above are pinned to it). Main keeps changing while you work; Claude measures and reproduces on a local copy of 74e34cf, so a finding in that code counts even if main has since changed it.
Read every file each page loads (HTML, CSS, JS, shaders).

List everything that runs at rest, every frame: requestAnimationFrame loops, CSS animations and what each one animates (transform/opacity run on the compositor; anything else repaints), filter and backdrop-filter under or on moving things, canvases (their size against devicePixelRatio and how often they redraw), WebGL (draw calls, overdraw, cost per pixel of each shader).
Then what runs on scroll and on a tap.
For each cost: estimate its milliseconds per frame on a mid-range phone and show the reasoning (pixel count x work per pixel, or calls x cost).
For each, give a TOGGLE (one CSS rule or one small JS change that removes only that cost, so Claude can measure it) and a FIX (the change that keeps the look and removes most of the cost).
Rank by estimated cost, largest first.

self_check: Every file:line is in the code as it is on main on the day you write (Claude opens every one).
Every claim says how Claude can see it for itself: a reproduction, a toggle or an input.
Nothing is padded: one real finding beats three guesses. A finding Claude cannot reproduce or measure counts against you.
The file is valid JSON (or the shape asked) and is named exactly as asked.
Each toggle removes one cost only, so its measured effect can be told apart.
tasks.done_when: 10 or more findings, ranked, each with a toggle and a fix.
checks: Claude applies each toggle on a phone-size copy of commit 74e34cf with the CPU slowed 4x and measures frames per second at rest and while scrolling: a finding counts when its toggle moves the number. Score: confirmed findings, minus wrong ones, plus how closely your ranking matches the measured order.
rejected_if: a file:line that does not exist or does not do what the row says
a finding that is the same as another with the words changed
more wrong findings than right ones
a file saved anywhere but the folder named here, or under another name
a toggle that removes several things at once
no arithmetic behind an estimate
tasks.review: Scored 9 (trial 3). 24 findings, every file:line exact on 74e34cf. Measured on a phone-size copy (software WebGL): Athenaeum's nebula pass 5 -> 20 fps with it off, the home sky still drawing under the menu 5 -> 15 fps, the menu-world shader the other large cost; your top three are the measured top three, and the hidden home sky is a find Claude had missed. One measured the wrong way: removing will-change on #ath-layer children dropped Athenaeum to 1 fps. The CSS items (blurs, filters, scanlines) were too small to tell apart in software rendering here; they stay on the list for a phone check. Details: docs/agents/trials/2026-11-20-gemini.md.

tasks.title: Nine particle shapes, one per door, as JavaScript functions
tasks.why: Pointing at a door bends the desk's particle field into that door's shape. Today the shapes are rough. Each door needs a shape that reads at a glance.
steps: Read how src/particles.js builds its targets.
Write one function per door: shapeTitan, shapeMidas, shapeHearth, shapeApollo, shapeHermes, shapeKairos, shapeIcarus, shapeArgus, shapeSylade.
Each is function(n, rand) returning a Float32Array of exactly n*3 numbers (x, y, z), every value between -1 and 1, using only rand() for randomness (so the same rand gives the same shape).

Shapes: Titan = a coin seen at 30 degrees with a raised rim; Midas = a rising stair of five steps; Hearth = a house with a pitched roof and a chimney; Apollo = a laurel wreath; Hermes = a winged envelope; Kairos = a clock face with two hands at 10:10; Icarus = one wing; Argus = an eye; Sylade = a standing figure in profile.
No imports, no DOM, no Three.js: plain functions in one file.

deliver.folder: Prometheus Hub/Pillars/Prometheus Hub (the desk)/incoming (AI drop files)/
deliver.shape: one .js file: export function shapeTitan(n, rand) {...} ... (9 exports)

tasks.done_when: 9 exported functions; each returns exactly n*3 numbers in [-1, 1] for n = 2000, 8000 and 24000, the same output for the same seed, and is recognisable in Claude's contact sheet.
checks: Claude runs each function in node at three sizes and checks length, range and determinism.
Claude renders all nine as point clouds from the front and at 30 degrees and looks at them.
rejected_if: any function that throws, returns the wrong length or a value outside [-1, 1]
a shape that is a sphere, cube or noise cloud with a label on it
Math.random() anywhere
